theoryTitle: Physics of Acoustic Beats & Fourier Analysis
theoryP1: Acoustic beats occur when two sound waves with slightly different frequencies interfere with each other. The interference alternates periodically between constructive (maximum loudness) and destructive (minimum loudness). The human ear perceives this as a single tone at the average frequency whose loudness throbs at the beat frequency f_beat = |f1 - f2|.
theoryP2: Musicians utilize beats for fine instrument tuning: when adjusting a string against a reference pitch, reducing the beat rate towards zero confirms that the frequencies are matching, achieving perfect unison.
theoryP3: According to Fourier's theorem (Joseph Fourier, 1822), any periodic waveform can be decomposed into or synthesized from a series of simple sine waves whose frequencies are integer multiples of the fundamental frequency. As more harmonics are included, the approximation sharpens, revealing the Gibbs overshoot phenomenon at abrupt edges.
